newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary 1996 beet harvest seen yielding surplus.
newsitem.headline: Hungary 1996 beet harvest seen yielding surplus.

text.p: Hungary's sugar harvest is likely to be higher than originally expected with some surplus beets likely to be exported, an industry official said on Monday.

"Although the sugar content per beet is relatively low, this is offset by the higher than expected root weight due to almost permanent rains since mid-August," Andras Angeli, chairman of the Sugar Industry Association, told Reuters.
Sugar content at the last test, released on September 27, was 14.1 percent, up from 13.5 percent two weeks earlier but lower than last year's figure of 14.3 percent.
Hungary's domestic sugar requirements will be around 480,000 tonnes given the need to replenish state reserves, Angeli said.
Heavy rains, although boosting root weight, have significantly delayed harvesting, he added.
"The delay is somewhere between two to two and a half weeks," he said, adding that this week all sugar factories will gear up to full capacity as the fields have dried out somewhat.
Angeli said a final estimate for beet production will be available on October 20. He did not specify where the surplus beets would be exported to.
In August the sugar industry association estimated production would be 4.3 million tonnes but Angeli said he estimates some 4.5 million tonnes.
Expected sugar output is between 460,000 and 480,000 tonnes, compared to 480,000 tonnes last year. --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
